_doc: ⚑ S209 / P7-48 — THE CLOSE'S MESSAGE (his, 2026-10-02: 'we are missing the information about SOGICE and why this is important, like the educational aspect that helps close the narrative… after the glitching of Maya maybe the computer should say "L will be waiting for the next update — coming soon"… then messages about the continued rise of violence against LGBTQIA+ people, and the continued existence of SOGICE'). Built from docs/reinterp/RESEARCH_CLOSE_MESSAGE_2026-10-02.md (every claim fetched and labelled there; the Commission's page and the FRA figures re-checked by me) with his notes: 'trans people' rather than the binary pair (FRA publishes figures for trans women and trans men only, so 'trans and gender diverse' would claim a number it did not publish); no search-results detail; the EU 'declined to propose a law'; his B6 line verbatim. FRAME VOICE: plain, no sensationalism, no graphic violence; the frame never plays. Shown after the eyes rise to the stars and before the panels open; each card holds ~9 s or until a press.
laptopLine: L will be waiting for the next update — coming soon.

cards.text: L is invented, but being told to change is not. A conversion practice is any attempt to change who someone loves, or who they are. In a European survey of more than 100,000 LGBTIQ people, one in four said someone had tried to change them. Most often it was words, and often it was family.

cards.text: For trans people it was nearly one in two, and three in four of those who went through it said they never agreed to it. That is why this piece ends with Maya: today the pressure to change falls twice as hard on trans people.

cards.text: Meridian is invented, but the movement behind it is not. Although many LGBT+ organisations support trans and gender-diverse people, the campaign against “gender ideology” has taken root inside the community itself: groups calling themselves feminist, or “LGB”, campaign against trans and gender-diverse people's rights. The campaign calls affirming trans young people “conversion”, and being trans a “social contagion”.
cards._docS357ao: ⚑ S357ao — HIS WORDING (12 Nov, on draft 2): 'Meridian is invented but the movement behind it is not. Although many LGBT+ orgs support Trans and Gender Diverse people, campaigns against “gender ideology” has taken root inside the community itself: groups calling themselves feminist, or “LGB”, campaign against Trans and Gender Diverse rights. Discriminatilating calling it "conversion", and "social contagion"'. Kept as his, with only these changes, for him to confirm: a comma after 'invented'; 'orgs' spelled out; 'campaigns … has' made one campaign so the verb agrees; 'trans and gender-diverse' in lower case like the other cards; 'rights' given its owners; his unfinished last sentence completed as 'The campaign calls affirming trans young people “conversion”, and being trans a “social contagion”.' Sources for that sentence: 'conversion' is the dossier's documentary card e4_offers#2 (an LGB-only group's letter to all MPs, 30 Mar 2021, and its email to clergy, 2 Feb 2022, that affirming a child is 'itself a form of conversion therapy'; asked that gender identity be kept out of the ban); The Hate Review's UK chapter (pp. 418, 422) records religious and so-called "gender critical" organisations formally opposing any ban covering gender identity. 'Social contagion' as the anti-gender movement's framing: The Hate Review (Belgium, p. 73: trans identities framed as a social contagion; France, p. 141: the Senate report framing gender-questioning youth as a social contagion driven by online influences). The subject is 'the campaign', not the LGB-only groups alone, because the KB documents 'conversion' for those groups and 'social contagion' for the movement. The clinical debate is not touched: the card reports how the campaign speaks, not what the evidence says (RESEARCH_ROGD_AND_FILTERS keeps both readings). Superseded wording below (_docS357am).
cards.accepted: his yes, 12 Nov 2026 ('Yes keep them!'; the Meridian card 'much better!!')
cards._docS357am: ⚑ S357am — DRAFT 2, after his direction on the S370 draft (12 Nov: 'I would put it more focused on the anti-gender and anti-gender-ideology aspect, and claim more directly — even inside of the LGBT+ community'). The claim is The Hate Review's own (Forbidden Colours, Sept 2026, p. 18, the so-called "gender critical" actors): essentially absent before 2015 and founded sharply after, mainly in Western and Northern Europe; they present themselves as feminist organisations or as "LGB organisations" and campaign against legal gender recognition and trans people's rights 'from a claimed position within'; 'anti-gender positions have taken root inside the very constituencies that have been targeted by the anti-gender movement'. Caveat kept from RESEARCH_CLOSE_MESSAGE §12: that section is an advocacy dataset and its framing is the authors'; the card cites it, so the claim is attributed on screen. Still no group named, and the last sentence keeps the inclusive services in the same breath (RESEARCH_LGB_REFUSAL §7), so it lands on the movement, never on lesbian, gay or bisexual people. The S370 draft read: 'Meridian is invented. Its rule is not: some groups that serve only lesbian, gay and bisexual people decide who they serve by sex recorded at birth, and turn trans people away. Many LGBT+ services kept their doors open.' The dossier phrasing stays his.
cards._docS370: ⚑ S370 / C4 — DRAFT, the dossier phrasing is Sérgio's (CLAUDE.md). His 11 Nov question: is it clear that Meridian turns trans people away? The card before this one already says the pressure to change falls more on trans people (FRA 2024: one in four, nearly one in two for trans people), so the UK survey's 13% vs 7% (marked [VERIFY SOURCE] in RESEARCH_2026_TRANS_PRESSURE §2.1, never opened at its own source) is NOT used. This card names the documented pattern behind Meridian (docs/reinterp/RESEARCH_LGB_REFUSAL_2026-10-31.md §1–2: LGB-only services defining eligibility by sex recorded at birth; the EHRC code of 5 Aug 2026) and, as that report's §7 asks, keeps the inclusive services on screen in the same breath, so the critique lands on the exclusion rule and never on lesbian, gay or bisexual people. No group is named on the card; the sources name what the KB documents.

cards.text: It does not end with a scandal. This piece followed it through four decades, each time in that decade's newest medium: a tape, a website, a feed, and now an AI that talks back. “Conversion therapy never goes away, no matter the scandals.”

cards.text: When a practice is banned by name, it changes its name. The UN's independent expert reported it in 2020: the same practices, renamed, offered again. You heard the names in this piece: “healing”, “freedom”, “restoration”. The words got softer. The ask stayed the same: change who you are.

The UN’s independent expert reported it in 2020: the same practices, renamed, offered again.'

cards.text: Some laws have changed. Seventeen countries ban conversion practices nationwide; in the EU, eight do. In 2026 more than a million Europeans asked the EU for a ban. It answered with a recommendation for 2027 that no country has to follow, and declined to propose a law.

cards.text: Behind the renaming is an organised movement. A 2026 review of 47 European countries found none in the lowest range of anti-gender campaigning, and none where it had declined in twenty-five years. It has moved from the street into courts and parliaments, and it now stops more equality measures than it fails to stop.

cards.text: Hostility is rising. In the EU survey, harassment of LGBTIQ people rose from 37% to 55% in four years; for trans people it was 69%. Fewer than one in five who are attacked report it anywhere official. A ban is a law on paper; safety is what happens on the street and online.
